h1: Picking an SEO agency for Melbourne
metaTitle: Who Is the Best SEO Agency in Melbourne?
metaDescription: No agency is best for every Melbourne business. The AUD-versus-offshore maths, the suburb-level search offshore teams miss, and when local wins out.
answer: No single agency is best for every Melbourne business. The real choice is local versus offshore: Australian agencies commonly quote AUD 2,000–10,000 a month, offshore teams a fraction of that. Pay the Melbourne premium when you need suburb-level local search, Australian media links or on-the-ground review work. Otherwise offshore handles technical and content fine.
takeaways: Nobody searches for "Melbourne". They search **Brunswick**, **Hawthorn**, **Dandenong** — and an offshore team that builds one Melbourne page has already lost.
Australian retainers cost more for structural reasons: **12% superannuation**, state payroll tax, and inner-Melbourne rent. That's the price of the postcode, not the price of the skill.
The overlap between India and Melbourne is **2.5 hours in winter and 1.5 in summer** — and it moves twice a year, because India doesn't do daylight saving.
Suburb names repeat across Australia. Richmond, Brighton and Kensington all exist in more than one state, and an offshore writer will get it wrong at least once.

sections.h2: "Best" isn't the question — local versus offshore is
body: Search this phrase and you'll get listicles. Most of those lists are paid placements or the publisher's own affiliate arrangements, which is why the same handful of names appear on all of them in a different order. They tell you who bought a slot, not who does good work.

The decision that actually matters is where the work gets produced. Some SEO tasks genuinely need a person in Victoria. Most don't. Once you sort your own requirements into those two piles, the shortlist writes itself and the price comparison stops being apples-to-oranges.
So start with the cost gap, because it's large enough to change what you can afford to do.

callout.title: About those "top 10 Melbourne SEO agencies" pages
callout.body: Ask any list publisher how an agency gets on it. If the answer involves a submission fee, a sponsorship tier or a reciprocal link, you're reading an ad. That's not illegal — it's just not research.

sections.h2: Why an Australian retainer costs what it costs
body: There's no published benchmark for Australian SEO retainers, so treat AUD 2,000–10,000 a month as the band of quotes you're likely to encounter for small and mid-size work rather than a survey figure. Enterprise programmes run well above it.
The gap between that and an Indian retainer isn't a quality gap. It's a cost-base gap, and it's mostly legislated.

callout.title: Ask where the work is produced
callout.body: "Which parts of this are done in your Melbourne office, and which are subcontracted?" A fair share of Australian agency content and link work is already produced offshore. That's fine — but it changes what the premium is buying.

sections.h2: Melbourne searches by suburb, not by city
body: This is the single biggest thing overseas teams get wrong. Greater Melbourne sprawls across hundreds of suburbs and an hour-plus drive end to end, and nobody types "plumber Melbourne" when they mean Coburg. They type the suburb, or they type nothing at all and let Google's location signal do the work.
That has three practical consequences for how a site should be built.
numbered: **Service-area pages need to be suburb- or cluster-level**, and they need to be genuinely different from each other. One thin page per suburb with the name swapped is scaled content, and Google treats it accordingly. Group by how people actually think — inner north, inner east, bayside, south-east — and write one real page per cluster.

**Locals use regional shorthand an outsider won't know.** "Inner north", "the bayside suburbs", "out east", "the south-east". If your copy reads like it was written from a map, it reads like it was written from a map.

**Suburb names repeat across states.** There's a Richmond in Melbourne, in Sydney and in Tasmania. Brighton exists in Victoria, South Australia and Queensland. An offshore writer working from a keyword tool will eventually publish a page aimed at the wrong Richmond.

**Your Google Business Profile does the heavy lifting for the map pack**, not your suburb pages. Get the category, service areas, hours, photos and review flow right first. See [local SEO services](/services/local-seo-services) for what that actually involves.

sections.h2: The .au signal and where Australian links come from
body: A `.com.au` domain is a trust signal to Australian buyers more than a ranking lever. It reads as "this is a real Australian business", and the reason it reads that way is that it's gated: auDA rules require an Australian presence — an ABN, ACN or Australian trademark — to hold one. The shorter direct `.au` namespace opened in 2022 and carries the same presence requirement. Check current rules with an accredited registrar before you plan around either.

The other Australian trust markers cost nothing and get skipped constantly: an ABN in the footer, an `03` phone number that a human answers, prices in AUD with GST treatment stated, and an Australian street address rather than a virtual office.

Links are where offshore engagements most often under-deliver. Australian media is concentrated in a small number of owners, and the Melbourne mastheads and city guides that matter run on relationships, not cold outreach from a different timezone. Sector directories and association memberships — your industry body, your chamber, your trade register — are slower but far more reliable, and an offshore team can chase those perfectly well.
bullets: **Review platforms differ from the US playbook.** Google reviews first, always. Then ProductReview.com.au for consumer categories, hipages, Oneflare and Airtasker for trades, RateMyAgent for property, HotDoc and HealthEngine for medical bookings. Yelp is close to irrelevant here.

**Health businesses have a compliance problem most agencies don't know about.** Practitioners registered with AHPRA face restrictions on using testimonials in advertising they control. A US-style review-generation campaign run at a Melbourne clinic can create a regulatory issue, not just a marketing one. Check the current AHPRA advertising guidelines before anyone builds a review funnel.

body: Melbourne runs AEST in winter and AEDT over summer. India sits at UTC+5:30 all year and doesn't observe daylight saving. So the gap is 4.5 hours for part of the year and 5.5 hours for the rest, and it shifts on Australian daylight-saving dates without warning if nobody's diarised it.

In practice that means a 9-to-5 Melbourne day overlaps an Indian working day by roughly two and a half hours in winter and an hour and a half in summer, and the overlap sits at the end of the Melbourne day. It works — a standing call at 4pm Melbourne is a very normal 11:30am in Bangalore — but it's a real constraint. Nothing gets answered same-day if you ask at 10am.

Two Victorian quirks worth putting in a shared calendar: the Melbourne Cup public holiday on the first Tuesday in November, and the AFL Grand Final holiday. An offshore team that schedules a launch on either has learned nothing about your market.

callout.title: The thing to negotiate up front
callout.body: Not "do you work Australian hours?" — almost nobody genuinely does. Ask instead: what's the guaranteed response window, who covers when the account lead is asleep, and what's the escalation path if the site breaks at 10am Melbourne time?

sections.h2: When Melbourne is worth the premium — and where we fit
body: Hire locally when your growth depends on relationships and physical presence: Australian digital PR, regulated categories where someone needs to understand AHPRA or ASIC rules first-hand, multi-location retail where reviews get collected in person, and tenders or partnerships where somebody expects to meet you.

Hire offshore when the constraint is capacity rather than proximity: technical SEO, Core Web Vitals, migrations, structured data, English content at volume, analytics and reporting. Crawling your site from Bangalore returns exactly the same data as crawling it from Fitzroy.

Our SEO retainers start at ₹75,000/mo, with smaller sites from ₹40,000/mo, ex-GST, month-to-month after the first quarter, and you keep every asset. We don't pretend to run Australian media relations from India — when a client needs it, we say so and it gets sourced locally. The wider trade-off is covered in [Indian agency versus international agency](/compare/indian-seo-agency-vs-international-agency), and the price comparison in [what SEO costs in India](/cost/seo-cost-in-india).

The one thing that doesn't change with the currency: we guarantee movement against your own frozen 90-day baseline of qualified organic leads, never a ranking position. Miss it in 90 days and we keep working free until we beat it.

faqs.q: How much does SEO cost in Melbourne?
faqs.a: Australian agencies commonly quote roughly AUD 2,000–10,000 a month for small and mid-size work, with enterprise programmes above that. There's no published benchmark, so treat that as an observed quote range. Offshore teams price well below it — ours start at ₹75,000/mo — because the cost base differs, not the work.

faqs.q: Do I need a .com.au domain to rank in Australia?
faqs.a: It helps trust more than rankings, and it's gated: auDA rules require an Australian presence such as an ABN, ACN or Australian trademark. A .com with an Australian Google Business Profile, an ABN on site, AUD pricing and Australian links performs fine. Check current registrar requirements before committing.

faqs.q: Can an Indian SEO agency work for a Melbourne business?
faqs.a: Yes, for technical work, English content, analytics and reporting. The constraint is the clock: 4.5 hours' difference in winter and 5.5 in summer, so you get roughly one to two and a half hours of genuine overlap. Australian media relations and in-person review collection still need someone local.

faqs.q: Should I build a page for every Melbourne suburb?
faqs.a: No. One thin page per suburb with the name swapped is scaled content and Google suppresses it. Build one substantial page per genuine service cluster — inner north, bayside, south-east — with real detail about how you serve it, and put the map-pack effort into your Google Business Profile instead.

faqs.q: Which review sites matter for SEO in Australia?
faqs.a: Google reviews first by a wide margin. After that it's category-specific: ProductReview.com.au for consumer brands, hipages, Oneflare and Airtasker for trades, RateMyAgent for property, HotDoc and HealthEngine for medical. Yelp barely registers. Health practitioners should check AHPRA advertising rules before running any review campaign.
